Language Models (Mostly) Know What They Know Kadavath arxiv

sources_considered.why: ICLR 2024 paper by Google DeepMind authors directly testing unaided self-correction of reasoning.
Anthropic study directly testing whether LLMs can evaluate the validity of their own answers.

evidence_items.publisher: arXiv / ICLR 2024 (Huang et al., Google DeepMind)

receipt.public_excerpt: LLMs struggle to self-correct their responses without external feedback, and at times, their performance even degrades after self-correction.

evidence_items.explanation: Supports the substance of the claim for reasoning: without external feedback, LLMs largely fail to check and fix their own reasoning, and sometimes make it worse.

receipt.public_excerpt: We find encouraging performance, calibration, and scaling for P(True) on a diverse array of tasks.

evidence_items.explanation: Large LLMs could estimate, with useful calibration, whether their own proposed answers were correct. That is a form of self-checking, which cuts against the absolute 'literally can't'.

unresolved_gaps: The studies use different tasks and models. Neither tests the exact general claim across all LLMs in the period.
How much self-evaluation ability counts as 'sanity-checking' is not defined.
